 Order

1. Revision petition is directed against the order dated 09.11.2022 passed by Ld MM-07 South West District, Dwarka in case titled as " TN Singh Yadav Vs. Chanda Yadav" bearing Ct. No.
4996794/2016 wherein complaint case instituted by revisionist was dismissed.

sentences.text: Brief facts 2.

Revisionist instituted a complaint case under Section 200 Cr.P.C alleging commission of offences punishable under Section 420/427/425/468/471/34 IPC on allegations that he purchased 75 sq yards land in the name of his wife Shanti Yadav out of a plot of 225 Sq. Yards from Sh. Hukum Singh located at Block E, Phase I, Qutub Vihar, New Delhi and the other part CR No. 97/2023 TN Singh Yadav Vs. ChandaYadav & Anr.
measuring 150 Sq. Yards

sentences.text: was purchased by respondent no.2 in the name of his wife Chanda Yadav.
In respect of sale all related documents that is GPA, Agreement to Sell, Affidavit and receipt of money of the plot was executed.
Revisionist kept these documents with him alongwith the chain of the said documents.
3. It is alleged that respondents in October 2013 asked revisionist for all documents of the said plot saying that they intended to construct a house on the divided part of 150 Sq. yards.
Accordingly, all documents pertaining to joint plot of 225 Sq. Yards were handed over to the respondents in good faith, being in cordial relations with respondents.

4. Revisionist alleged that in the mid of January 2014, he intended to construct a house on the portion of 75 Sq. Yards and he requested and asked the respondents to handover all the CR No.
97/2023 TN Singh Yadav Vs. ChandaYadav & Anr.
related original documents pertaining to the said plot but respondents avoided to hand over the above said documents on one pretext or the other .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Revisionist averred that he further requested and asked respondents to hand over original documents but respondents intently ignored.
Thereafter revisionist filed a complaint before PS Chhawla as DD No. 21B dated 26.01.2014.
Upon this SI Rajesh Kumar called both the parties and asked respondents to show the relevant documents.
Respondent no.2 produced some documents and revisionist requested SI to provide the photocopy of the said documents but documents were not provided to him.
Revisionist alleged that he made many complaint to P.S. Chhawla but no action was taken by the police.

T.N. Singh Yadav deposed on the lines of the allegations made in the complaint.

2 as Ex CW1/A & B and relied upon some photocopies of documents as Mark A to H.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: CW2 Shanti Yadav proved a copy of Civil suit as Ex CW2/A in which Ashok showed address of the plot and a receipt of Rs 4 lac as Ex CW2/B.
CW3 Pradeep Patial son of Hukum Singh (alleged seller) proved a receipt Ex CW3/A executed by his father and deposed that 75 sq yards of plot was sold to revisionist no.2 by his father.
8. Ld Trial Court after considering the material on record dismissed the complaint case instituted by revisionists.
CR No. 97/2023 TN Singh Yadav Vs. ChandaYadav & Anr.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Grounds of Revision 9.
Revisionists preferred the revision petition on the ground that Ld Trial Court committed an error while discarding receipt Ex CW3/A.
It is submitted that said receipt as well as deposition of CW3 Pradeep Patial (son of seller) would show that 75 sq. yards of land was sold to the revisionist no.2 by Hukum Singh.
It is submitted that while arriving at conclusion, Ld Trial Court did not consider the marked documents relied upon by the revisionists in order to prove their title over the plot.
It is alleged that respondents forged documents to possess the portion of land which is owned by revisionist no.2 and also filed a Civil suit on the basis of those documents.
Hence, revisionists prayed that impugned order be set-aside.
Respondent's Contention 10.

On the other hand respondents in their reply submitted that they are absolute owner of the property in question by virtue of CR No. 97/2023 TN Singh Yadav Vs. ChandaYadav & Anr.
valid documents in their favor.

entities.text: CR No. 97/2023 TN Singh Yadav Vs. ChandaYadav & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that respondent no.1 purchased a plot No.C- 33, Area Measuring 150 square yards at Khasra No.16/25 out of total 225 square yard from one Sh. Hukum Singh on 06.02.2001 and remaining part of the said land i.e. 75 square yards was purchased by respondent no.2 in his name on 04.04.2001.
It is further submitted that respondents are having possession in their properties since day of purchase and between 2013 to 2014 both properties were constructed.

It is submitted that revisionists are allegedly claiming right in the property in the portion of 75 square yards without any valid documents in their favor and they have falsely made complaints to the police.
11. I have heard the rival contentions and have gone through the record.
CR No. 97/2023 TN Singh Yadav Vs. ChandaYadav & Anr.

entities.text: TN Singh Yadav Vs. ChandaYadav & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Analysis 12.
In order to establish that respondents have cheated them, revisionists must show that revisionist no.2 is owner of 75 sq. yards land.
Revisionists have failed to produce any documents on record which shows title of revisionist no.2 over plot in question.

Only a receipt Ex CW3/A has been proved on record allegedly executed by Hukum Singh, owner of the plot but presuming receipt to be Cr No. 97/2023 Tn Singh Yadav vs . Chandayadav & Anr. on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100883681/
3

entities.text: Cr No. 97/2023 Tn Singh Yadav vs . Chandayadav & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
genuine documents even then this receipt doesn't confer title of the said plot to the revisionist no.2.
13.
More so, as noted by Ld Trial Court receipt Ex CW3/A pertains to entire 225 sq. yards of the land belonging to Hukum Singh whereas, revisionists claims that they purchased only 75 sq. yards.
Receipt also indicates there is some balance payment.

There is absolutely no evidence on record that any title CR No. 97/2023 TN Singh Yadav Vs. ChandaYadav & Anr.
document was executed in favor of revisionist no.2.

entities.text: TN Singh Yadav Vs. ChandaYadav & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no assertion by revisionists that they were ever put to possession of the property.
In absence, of any material on record Ld. Trial Court rightly held that there is no material on record that revisionists were deprived or dispossessed from their land.
14. As stated above, revisionists neither summoned any witness to the alleged sale transaction between him and Hukum Singh nor any Registrar/ Notary was examined.
There is no document on record which substantiate the allegations of forgery as well.

14. Though revisionist has also filed an application U/s 397 Cr.P.C. thereby stating that he may be allowed to lead additional evidence in the present case but revisionists did not mention that what sort of evidence they want to produce and who are the CR No. 97/2023 TN Singh Yadav Vs.
ChandaYadav & Anr.
witnesses they intend to examine.

entities.text:
TN Singh Yadav Vs.
ChandaYadav & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Application lacks material particulars and has no merits at all and hence it stands dismissed.

15. In view of the above discussions, it is concluded that Ld. Trial Court has rightly reached to the conclusion that revisionists have failed to adduce any evidence which substantiates the allegations made by them against the respondents.
16. Ld. Trial Court has rightly appreciated and analyzed the pre-summoning evidence led by revisionists.
There is no illegality and infirmity in the impugned order.
Revision petition lacks merit and accordingly, same stands dismissed.
TCR be sent back along with copy of this order.
File be consigned to record room.
Announced in the open court on 19th August 2023.
